authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO / OMPI) / Patent Cooperation Treaty
title: PCT Article 1 & 3 - Purpose of the PCT and The International Application
text: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) Article 1 & 3: The States party to this Treaty constitute a Union for cooperation in the filing, searching, and examination, of applications for the protection of inventions. Applications for the protection of inventions in any of the Contracting States may be filed as international applications under this Treaty. The PCT provides a unified procedure for filing patent applications to protect inventions across member countries through a single international application filed with a Receiving Office.

title: PCT Article 18 & Rule 43 - The International Search Report (ISR)
text: PCT Article 18 The International Search Report: (1) The international search shall be carried out by the International Searching Authority (ISA). The international search report (ISR) shall be established within the prescribed time limit. (2) The ISR contains citations of prior art documents (patent publications, scientific articles) deemed relevant to the novelty and inventive step of the claimed invention, categorized as X (novelty-destroying alone), Y (obvious in combination), or A (technological background).

authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) / PCT Regulations
title: PCT Rule 43bis & Article 33 - Written Opinion of the ISA (WO-ISA) and Patentability Standards
text: PCT Rule 43bis Written Opinion of the International Searching Authority (WO-ISA): Together with the international search report, the ISA establishes a written opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, involve an inventive step (non-obviousness), and be industrially applicable under Article 33. The written opinion provides the applicant with a preliminary non-binding evaluation of patentability before incurring national phase entry expenses.

title: PCT Articles 21 & 22 - International Publication and National Phase Entry
text: PCT Article 21 & 22 International Publication and National Phase: Article 21: The International Bureau publishes international applications promptly after 18 months from priority date (WO publication). Published WO documents constitute prior art worldwide. Article 22: Within 30 or 31 months from priority date, the applicant must enter the national phase before designated national patent offices. The PCT does NOT grant an 'international patent' or 'worldwide patent'. A PCT filing only reserves the right to seek individual national grants.

authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) / International IP Scope
title: WIPO / PCT Scope Clarification - International Procedure vs Sovereign Sales Jurisdiction
text: WIPO PCT Legal Scope Boundary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) represent an international intellectual property search and application framework, NOT a sovereign nation, domestic market, or commercial sales territory. You cannot 'sell', 'market', or 'commercially distribute' an Ayurvedic or health product in 'WO'. Market entry, regulatory approval, health authority clearance (FDA, MHLW, CDSCO, EMA), and patent enforcement must be pursued in individual sovereign nations (IN, US, JP, EP) upon national phase entry.

authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) / PCT Chapter II
title: PCT Chapter II (Articles 31 to 35) & Rule 66 - International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP / Chapter II Demand)
text: PCT Chapter II (Articles 31 to 35) International Preliminary Examination and the International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP): On the demand of the applicant, the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) carries out an international preliminary examination under Chapter II of the PCT. The objective is to formulate a preliminary and non-binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (to be non-obvious), and to be industrially applicable under Article 33. The final report established under Article 35 is known as the International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP Chapter II). If no Chapter II demand is filed, the International Bureau converts the WO-ISA into the IPRP (Chapter I) upon 30 months.

authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO / OMPI) / Patent Cooperation Treaty
title: PCT Article 19 - Amendment of the Claims Before the International Bureau
text: PCT Article 19 Amendment of the Claims Before the International Bureau: (1) The applicant shall, after having received the international search report, be entitled on one occasion to amend the claims of the international application by filing amendments with the International Bureau within 2 months from the date of transmittal of the ISR or 16 months from the priority date, whichever expires later. (2) The amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. This allows applicants to narrow botanical or chemical formulation claims to overcome novelty (X) or obviousness (Y) citations before international publication under Article 21.
